title: Win64 -game dies in ~20s on 'Failed to create graphics pipeline' — every visual row blocked
description:
Found by the Win64/D3D12 pass 2026-08-03 (docs/passport/2026-08-vacuus-win64-results.md, commit 31b0628). THE reason 13 of 15 matrix rows are 'not run': no -game session survives long enough to show anything.

WHAT IS VERIFIED (not inferred): every -game session dies in ~20 seconds on 'Failed to create graphics pipeline' followed by a fatal. It is a PSO-CREATION failure, not a shader-compile failure -- 'LogShaderCompilers: Error' appears ZERO times in the logs. It reproduces. The engine itself renders fine: the one screenshot that survived shows the template level under D3D12 (sky, mannequin with a real shadow, green floor, brick walls) and NO VaCuus UI anywhere in the frame. The input layout in the failing description (offsets 0/8/12) is the RmlUi vertex.

WHAT IS INFERRED, NOT PROVEN: that the failing PSO is ours. Shader names print as <unknown> in the D3D12 error path, so attribution rests on the vertex layout alone. Establish that first -- if it is not ours, this bead changes shape entirely.

CONTEXT THAT MAKES IT ODD: the same shaders and the same replay path work on Linux/Vulkan (SM6) and macOS/Metal (SM5). Win64 bound SM6 on real hardware (RTX 2080 SUPER) -- the first SM6 execution of this code anywhere. So the suspect list starts with whatever differs at SM6/D3D12: the vertex declaration, blend/depth state, the composite permutation's render-target format, or a root-signature/binding-tier constraint the other two RHIs do not impose.

FIRST MOVES for whoever picks this up: turn on D3D12 validation and the debug layer to get a real reason string instead of the generic failure; get shader names to print (or bisect by disabling draws) to settle the attribution question; and check whether it is the UI pass, the composite, or the material pair by running a document that uses only one of them.

BLOCKS: the entire Win64 column of the manual matrix and the perf passport, the memory-mapped bundle observation (Win64 is the ONLY platform where that branch executes), the Win64 disk literal, and the IME row (bead akj.6.19).

title: UVaCuusWidget is Private and unexported — the documented UMG route is dead for any buyer who does not compile our source
description:
Found by the adversarial verifier of the binary-delivery simulation (workflow wv490rkeo, 2026-08-03), confirmed by hand: Source/VaCuusRender/Private/VaCuusUMGWidget.h — the header is under Private/, and the class is declared 'class UVaCuusWidget : public UWidget' with NO VACUUSRENDER_API anywhere in the file. VaCuusRender/Public/ contains only VaCuusCommandBuffer.h and VaCuusReplayRenderer.h.

CONSEQUENCE, measured on the shipped artifact: symbol probe of the delivered libUnrealEditor-VaCuusRender.so found Z_Construct_UClass_UVaCuusWidget exported (so the UCLASS registers and BLUEPRINT use works), but UVaCuusWidget:: members = 0 exported and 0 in the full symbol table. A buyer's C++ cannot include the header (Private) and cannot link the class (unexported). The second documented route is dead the same way: UVaCuusSubsystem::CreateView(TUniquePtr<IVaCuusDocumentHost>, FIntPoint) is public, but BOTH available host implementations -- FVaCuusRmlDocumentHost and SVaCuusWidget -- are Private/. So a C++ buyer has a public factory and no way to construct its argument.

This never surfaced before because every consumer so far (VcHost, VaCuusDemo, VaCuusUserDemo) compiles the plugin from source in-tree, where Private/ is reachable and export macros are irrelevant.

FIX SHAPE: move VaCuusUMGWidget.h to VaCuusRender/Public/ with VACUUSRENDER_API on the class; decide and publish ONE supported C++ host route (either export a concrete host, or ship a small public factory that returns an opaque handle); then re-run the binary simulation's C++ leg to prove a buyer can drive the plugin from code. Until then docs/buyer/setup.md's 'First document' section describes an API that a binary-delivery buyer cannot use.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: Fixed and merged 2026-08-03 (91f14a0, fix 63742dd). BOTH host classes were affected: UVaCuusWidget AND UVaCuusWorldComponent each exported ZERO members. Mechanism verified with a standalone clang experiment: -fvisibility-ms-compat (LinuxToolChain.cs:437-440) leaves types default but hides functions, while UHT stamps the module API macro on the class registrar regardless — so the UCLASS registered and Blueprint worked while every member stayed invisible to a linker. FIX: both headers Private -> Public with VACUUSRENDER_API; UMG + VaCuus promoted to PublicDependencyModuleNames; the surface decision recorded in VaCuusRender.Build.cs. EVIDENCE: nm -D on delivered artifacts — UVaCuusWidget 0->21, UVaCuusWorldComponent 0->47, FVaCuusRmlDocumentHost 0->0; a real consumer project linking the delivered .so, deliberately calling only NON-virtual out-of-line members (virtuals ride the vtable that ms-compat exports anyway, so a virtual-only probe would have passed while the bug was live); three-leg restore-the-bug, one of which refuted the obvious guess (demoting UMG to a private dep still COMPILES — the include path leaks transitively — and dies at link on UWidget::TakeWidget). DELIBERATE NON-FIX: no constructible IVaCuusDocumentHost exported, since that drags the render backend in as supported ABI at v0.1; CreateView is now documented as the extension seam it actually is. GATE: Tools/api_export_check.sh, seen to fail on the pre-fix package (2 violations, exit 1) and pass after — no automation test can catch this class, because in-process tests link against the module under test.

title: The Fab package ships no binaries, no README and no docs — a Blueprint-only buyer cannot use the product
description:
Found by the adversarial verifier of the 2026-08-02 buyer-install simulation (workflow warwptkvj), which graded the install GREEN and then had its own verdict overturned. Three shipping-shape defects, each confirmed against the produced artifact /w/Unreal/FabDryRun2/Package (978 files, 9.76 MiB unpacked, 2.96 MiB zipped) and engine source:

(1) ZERO BINARIES, AND setup.md DOES NOT SAY SO. Package top level is Content/ Resources/ Shaders/ Source/ VaCuus.uplugin Web/ -- no Binaries/. This is deliberate (FilterPlugin.ini excludes them under Fab's source-only mandate) but it means a BLUEPRINT-ONLY BUYER CANNOT USE THE PRODUCT AT ALL: no C++ toolchain, no way to compile 978 source files. docs/buyer/setup.md section 1 step 1 says only 'Drop the plugin into <Project>/Plugins/VaCuus'. This is the biggest first-day blocker in the product and it is documented nowhere. Decide: ship prebuilt binaries for the supported platforms (changes the Fab listing category and the FilterPlugin rules), or state the C++-project requirement prominently in setup.md AND the Fab listing.

(2) README.md AND Config/ DO NOT SHIP. BuildPluginCommand's default filter has no rule for root files other than the descriptor (BuildPluginCommand.Automation.cs:459-472). So the one document that tells a buyer to enable the plugin, and that carries the symlink/UBA warning, is exactly what they never receive. docs/buyer/*.md ship nowhere either -- the simulation READ them from our dev tree, which is finding C2: the experience graded green was a documented buyer's, not a real buyer's.

(3) BuildPlugin STRIPS 'EnabledByDefault': true (NewDescriptor.bEnabledByDefault = null, BuildPluginCommand.Automation.cs:434-445) and sets EngineVersion 5.8.0 + Installed true. The buyer's copy is NOT enabled by default; they must enable it in Edit->Plugins or their .uproject. Nothing tells them.

ALSO WORTH FIXING WHILE HERE: shipped test fixtures hardcode our internal project name -- VaCuusEditor/Private/Tests/VaCuusLiveReloadTest.cpp:206 has '../../../VcHost/Content/DevUI/m1_hud.rcss' and VaCuusBundle.cpp:392 cites 'VcHost/Config/DefaultEditor.ini:14'. Buyers read those.

FIX SHAPE: FilterPlugin.ini gains README.md + a shipped docs/ subset (setup, gotchas, perf-guide, rcss-matrix); setup.md gains a 'What you receive / what you need' first section stating the C++ requirement, the not-enabled-by-default step, and the project-side content staging rule (DirectoriesToAlwaysStageAsUFS(Path="DevUI") -- the plugin's RuntimeDependencies glob only covers $(PluginDir), so a buyer's OWN DevUI content does not stage; the simulation hit this and so did the VaCuusDemo packaging the same day).

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
PREMISE CORRECTED BY THE OWNER (2026-08-03), and it invalidates finding (1) plus the M6 decision behind it. Fab COMPILES the plugin itself and delivers BINARIES to the buyer, installed into the ENGINE (Engine/Plugins/Marketplace/<Name>), not source into the project. So: a Blueprint-only buyer CAN use the product — that half of this bead is wrong and withdrawn. What survives, and what this re-opens:

STILL VALID: README.md and Config/ do not ship (BuildPluginCommand.Automation.cs:459-472 has no root-file rule) — the doc that explains enabling the plugin never reaches the buyer; BuildPlugin strips EnabledByDefault (:434-445); shipped test fixtures hardcode our internal project name (VaCuusLiveReloadTest.cpp:206 '../../../VcHost/...', VaCuusBundle.cpp:392); the project-side content staging rule (DirectoriesToAlwaysStageAsUFS) is undocumented for buyers.

RE-OPENED: M6 Task 6 added '-/Binaries/...' and '-/Intermediate/...' to Config/FilterPlugin.ini on the reasoning 'Fab is source-only, a shipped .so is what the scan exists to stop'. That reasoning rests on the same wrong premise. For a Fab-built plugin the buyer NEEDS Binaries/ and Intermediate/Build/<Platform>/<Target>/Inc/ (the UHT-generated headers) — that is what makes an installed plugin usable without compiling. The exclusions must be revisited: decide what the SELLER uploads versus what the BUYER receives, and make FilterPlugin match the upload contract rather than a guess about it. The fab_scan ELF/EXTENSION classes also need a rule that distinguishes 'a .so that must not be in the source upload' from 'a .so that legitimately ships in a built plugin'.

Superseded by the correction: the 'ship prebuilt binaries or state the C++ requirement' fix shape. The real question is narrower — upload contract vs delivery contract.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
BINARY-DELIVERY SIMULATION RESULTS (workflow wv490rkeo, 2026-08-03) — the owner's premise confirmed, and the shape that works is now pinned to engine source.

THE MECHANISM, verified verbatim in UBT: for a plugin under <Project>/Plugins/, RulesCompiler.cs:402 hardcodes bReadOnly: Unreal.IsProjectInstalled() -- false on any non-mod-kit engine -- and RulesAssembly.cs:573 sets bUsePrecompiled = bReadOnly, so the UEBuildBinary.cs:267-271 precompiled early-out NEVER fires and all five modules recompile. Measured: 236 build actions, 233 of them ours, ~10 minutes, full C++ toolchain required, the buyer's 210 MiB download overwritten. The -UsePrecompiled flag is inert here (two action JSONs identical but for env-var ordering). By contrast RulesCompiler.cs:100 gives a MARKETPLACE (engine) plugin bUsePrecompiled = IsEngineInstalled() || bUsePrecompiled -- so ENGINE INSTALL ON A LAUNCHER ENGINE IS THE ONLY SHAPE WHERE THE DELIVERED BINARIES ARE ACCEPTED. That is exactly what Fab does; the owner was right and this run proves why no other shape substitutes.

RUNTIME IS FINE: the delivered .so loaded by path with no version complaint and rendered the full M1 HUD without a build. The problem is UBT's decision, not our binaries.

THE BINARY ARTIFACT (/w/Unreal/FabDryRun3/Package): 1520 files / 209.99 MiB vs the source-only 978 / 9.76 MiB. Binaries/Linux = 16 files / 50.90 MiB, of which .debug + .sym = 42.4 MiB (83% of Binaries, 20% of the package) -- split-DWARF for OUR build of OUR modules, embedding our directory tree, undebuggable by a buyer. Lever: FilterPlugin.ini rides in the source upload and BPC:474-482 reads it on EVERY BuildPlugin invocation including Fab's, so -/Binaries/.../*.debug and *.sym should strip 42 MiB from the buyer's download (inference from :474-482, to confirm at upload time). Intermediate = 526 files / 149 MiB: 68 UHT generated headers plus 458 monolithic UnrealGame .o/.precompiled -- the latter unusable twice over (app name UnrealGame vs the target's UnrealEditor, and the shipped headers carry FID_FabDryRun3_... build-path macros so every buyer regenerates them anyway).

ALSO: the artifact ships 57 test .cpp (1.27 MiB) inside 12 MB of Source/ -- every buyer compiles our entire test suite, which is most of those 233 actions. setup.md offers no way to exclude it. And the 7 shipped files carrying our internal 'VcHost' name (VaCuusLiveReloadTest.cpp:206 literal + comments) reach every buyer.

TASKS THIS BEAD NOW OWNS: (1) setup.md gains an INSTALL MATRIX -- engine/Marketplace on a Launcher engine = binaries accepted; project Plugins/ = always rebuilt, C++ toolchain required, state the ~10 min cost; (2) FilterPlugin.ini: strip .debug/.sym, decide on the monolithic .o (dead weight in the observed shapes), decide whether Private/Tests ships; (3) README.md + a docs subset must ship; (4) EnabledByDefault is DELETED by BPC:434-445 -- setup.md must state the enable step as mandatory, not optional. Split into separate beads at implementation time if it gets unwieldy. Blocking product bug found alongside: VaCuus-dgl.

title: stat vacuus crashes the game the instant the group is enabled — silent death, crash pipeline broken
description: Found by the owner 2026-08-02 typing 'stat vacuus' into the running lobby demo console; REPRODUCED in VcHost (-game offscreen, -ExecCmds 'vacuus.RefHud, stat vacuus,') — plugin-wide, not demo-specific. Signature: the process dies within a frame of the group being enabled, the log ends mid-flight with no Fatal/callstack, no coredump lands (unlike the same session's Vulkan-OOM crashes, which dumped normally), and the exit status is 127 — read as the engine crash handler exec'ing the MISSING CrashReportClient binary (FUnixPlatformProcess::CreateProc 'File does not exist' seen in earlier logs), which destroys the evidence. Suspicion to verify with the gdb run: our VACUUS_PERF_SCOPE maps to SCOPE_CYCLE_COUNTER on THREE threads incl. the plugin's own UI thread; 'stat vacuus' turning collection on for the group is the first time the stats system ever receives messages from that thread in this codebase -- no automation test has ever enabled a stat group at runtime (the whole passport ran on the in-house PerfLog). The fix must land with a restore-the-bug automation test that ENABLES the group ('stat vacuus' via Exec) with live views and survives N frames, plus a CLAUDE.md/known-issues note about the missing CrashReportClient masking every hard crash on this machine.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: INVESTIGATION COMPLETE — VaCuus EXONERATED. Evidence chain, all steps reproducible: (1) owner's windowed lobby demo died on typing 'stat vacuus'; (2) reproduced in VcHost with '-ExecCmds vacuus.RefHud, stat vacuus,' — plugin-wide; (3) gdb: NO signal ever raised — the process calls exit_group(127) itself; (4) exit_group backtrace: _dl_fatal_printf (ld-linux) <- FThreadStats::AddStatMessage (StatsSystemTypes.h:1261) <- SCOPE_CYCLE_COUNTER in FXmppModule::Tick — ENGINE module, first stat message after master-enable; (5) CONTROL: 'stat slate' with zero VaCuus scopes exits 127 identically — any group-stat enable kills any UE process on this machine; (6) GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.rtld.optional_static_tls titration: 16/32/48/64 KB still 127; 98/128 KB break 128KB-stack thread creation at boot (OnlineSubsystemNull.cpp:307 check + stack-overflow SIGSEGV) — NO working dose exists, the deficit and the stack constraint overlap; (7) UBT already mitigates the class for everything it builds: -ftls-model=local-dynamic on all DLL modules (LinuxToolChain.cs:529-531, incl. our plugin) — the trigger is outside UBT-built code (prebuilt/system lib IE-TLS lazily resolved on the stats path) on Arch glibc 2.43+r37; (8) the missing CrashReportClient turns every such death into a silent no-core no-log exit — that masking cost half the investigation. DISPOSITION: environment/engine issue, not ours; owner machine avoids group stats (vacuus PerfLog is the project's instrument and covers every measurement need); buyer-facing note in gotchas (LTS-distro glibc likely unaffected — older surplus arithmetic); revisit only if a buyer reproduces on a supported distro. Sources: UE Linux Known Issues (static TLS exhaustion class), LinuxToolChain.cs local-dynamic comment.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: SCOPE CORRECTED after owner pushback ('у меня все работало до этого со статом' — he was right, my first write-up over-claimed). Four separate 60-second runs: (a) modular editor -game + 'stat slate' with VaCuus DISABLED -> dead 127; (b) modular + 'stat vacuus' -> dead 127; (c) modular + 'stat fps' -> LIVES (draws its own counter, never master-enables collection — this is what the owner remembers using); (d) STAGED MONOLITHIC VcHost + 'stat vacuus' -> LIVES (no dlopen, no static-TLS pressure). Blast radius is therefore the dev-loop MODULAR binary only; packaged games are immune by construction, which also defuses the buyer-facing angle. ROOT CAUSE REMAINS OPEN: the owner reports group stats working in the editor previously; glibc updated 2026-06-30 (2.43+r22 -> 2.43+r37) but the causal link is UNVERIFIED — the honest next experiment is a repro under the previous glibc from the pacman cache (fakechroot/container), which has not been run. title: Packaged game: the hud model never binds — [Rml] 'Could not locate data model' in the cooked Development build
description: Found by the M5 packaged-game gate (first Development BuildCookRun, 2026-08-01). In the staged Linux Development build, vacuus.M4Demo boots, m4_hud_logic.js runs from the pak, but the model bind never happens: no 'model hud bound on the UI thread' line, and frame 1 logs [Rml] Error: Could not locate data model 'hud' in element body < #root#VaCuusView1 — binding expressions are dead in the packaged game while the same flow works in editor -game (bind logs before the document attach). Ordering clue: in packaged, the attach error fires at frame [1] and 'View 1 loaded the VFS document' at [2]; in editor both bind and load land at [1] with bind first. The enqueue order is FIFO from one producer (StartModelDriver's BindModel is called before View->LoadDocument in Toggle, VaCuusRender.cpp:754-770), so either BindModel was refused at ENQUEUE time (the bRegistered gate? a Verbose-only refusal?) or the packaged startup drains commands across different frames in a way that lets the attach precede the bind. Repro: RunUAT BuildCookRun -platform=Linux -clientconfig=Development -build -cook -stage -pak; run StagedBuilds/Linux/VcHost.sh -RenderOffscreen -ForceRes -resx=1280 -resy=720 -ExecCmds=vacuus.M4Demo -log; grep the staged VcHost/Saved/Logs/VcHost.log.

title: Only PNG/JPEG/UEJPEG are safe to request as RGBA8; .bmp and .dds crash the editor
description: PRE-EXISTING since M1, found by the Task 11 re-review, VERIFIED against engine source by the controller. LoadTexture passes the format straight from IImageWrapperModule::DetectImageFormat to CreateImageWrapper and then calls GetRaw(ERGBFormat::RGBA, 8, ...). DetectImageFormat can return 11 formats, and the wrappers do NOT all honour the requested format: FATAL -- BmpImageWrapper.cpp:66-70 does check(InFormat == ERGBFormat::BGRA); check(InBitDepth == 8). DdsImageWrapper.cpp:177-178 does check(InFormat == GetFormat()); check(InBitDepth == GetBitDepth()). check() is fatal in every DO_CHECK build, i.e. Development Editor. So a document containing matches the 'BM' magic (ImageWrapperModule.cpp:175-177), passes the probe, and then HARD-CRASHES THE EDITOR from a decode worker thread. Same for any .dds, and for an .ico whose sub-image is BMP (IcoImageWrapper.cpp:89-98 delegates). SILENT WRONG COLOURS -- TgaImageWrapper.cpp:133-141 ignores InFormat and always writes BGRA order. Byte count is W*H*4 so every validation passes; red and blue are swapped with no diagnostic. INVISIBLE -- grayscale UEJPEG (see 6.30) yields W*H bytes and is rejected by the byte-count check. GRACEFUL ALREADY -- EXR, HDR, TIFF all refuse an 8-bit RGBA request and fail cleanly. FIX (one if, and it is the recommended workaround rather than a real fix): whitelist the detected format to {PNG, JPEG, UEJPEG} immediately after DetectImageFormat and log 'unsupported image format' for the rest. That closes the crash, closes the TGA colour swap, turns the grayscale-UEJPEG case into an honest 'unsupported format' message instead of 'the decoder disagreed with itself', and makes the concurrency and GetRaw-caveat comment blocks true as written instead of true-for-two-formats. The real fix upstream would be GetRawImage(FImage&) plus channel-order conversion in the plugin, which is a wider change (it returns ERawImageFormat terms, BGRA8 here).
design: Whitelist after DetectImageFormat. Do NOT try to support BMP/DDS/TGA by requesting BGRA and swizzling -- that spreads channel-order knowledge through the pipeline, whose contract is RGBA premultiplied everywhere.
acceptance_criteria: A document referencing a .bmp, .dds or .tga logs 'unsupported image format' and renders a transparent placeholder instead of crashing or showing swapped channels; a test covers at least the BMP case.
close_reason:
Fixed in d9a9ba4 (Task 11 second fix pass).

6.31: LoadTexture now whitelists {PNG, JPEG, UEJPEG} immediately after DetectImageFormat; anything else gets a Warning naming the file and the format and returns handle 0. The crash was REPRODUCED before the fix, with a real backtrace from a decode worker: 'Assertion failed: InFormat == ERGBFormat::BGRA [BmpImageWrapper.cpp:69]' via FBmpImageWrapper::UncompressBMPData <- Uncompress <- FImageWrapperBase::GetRaw <- IImageWrapper::GetRaw <- LoadTexture's decode lambda <- FScheduler::WorkerLoop. Process aborted at exit 139 with 25 of 31 tests completed. After the whitelist: 31/31, exit 0.

Tests cover BMP *and* TGA, both built with the engine's own encoders. TGA was included deliberately: it is the silent R/B-swap case rather than the crash case, so a test covering only BMP would not have pinned the whitelist's shape.

Labelled a workaround in the comment, with the real fix (GetRawImage(FImage&) plus channel-order conversion in the plugin) cited and scoped out.

6.30: grayscale UEJPEG is now refused at the PROBE on Probe->GetFormat() != ERGBFormat::RGBA, scoped to UEJPEG -- grayscale PNG and JPEG also report Gray and both decode correctly, so an unscoped test would have refused working images. With that gone, the SizeMismatch failure message is honest by construction (nothing can reach it claiming the decoder disagreed with itself).

6.28: all three items done -- the texture-release wording now says 'render-manager teardown, not on document close' with the RenderManager citations; the test-only API and its backing member/Add/prune are behind WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS; the same-buffer ordering note is at the drain site and in the test.

Zero impact on existing fixtures or the demo: all fixtures are PNG/JPEG, the fake-.png case is plain text and is refused by the Invalid branch before the whitelist, and m1_hud.rml's only image is a 64x64 8-bit RGBA PNG (verified). Swept the plugin for other image references -- the only other hits are CSS class names.

title: Packaging: loose Content/DevUI documents are not staged (FilterPlugin.ini is stock)
description: Task 10: Config/FilterPlugin.ini is still the stock template, so a cooked build stages no .rml/.rcss/fonts/images under either content root and will find no documents at runtime. Needs FilterPlugin.ini entries (or the UVaCuusBundle cook path from spec §9, which is M6 scope). Blocking for any packaged demo.
notes:
PREMISE OVERTURNED by the Task 14 implementer, verified against AutomationTool source. This bead said a stock FilterPlugin.ini meant a cooked build would stage no UI documents. That was wrong on the mechanism:

- Config/FilterPlugin.ini has exactly ONE consumer in the entire engine -- RunUAT BuildPlugin (BuildPluginCommand.Automation.cs:453 reads it, :472 loads it). The string appears in no other AutomationTool file. Neither CopyBuildToStagingDirectory nor DeploymentContext touches it. It could NEVER have affected a cooked game.
- For BuildPlugin, /Content/... is already in the DEFAULT filter (:464), alongside /Shaders/... (:466) and /Source/... (:467). The DevUI documents were never missing from a plugin zip either.
- ProjectPackagingSettings' DirectoriesToAlwaysStageAsUFS resolves against the PROJECT's content root (CopyBuildToStagingDirectory.Automation.cs:2054), never a plugin's -- so that was not the answer either.

FilterPlugin.ini was therefore deliberately left EMPTY with the finding recorded in it: adding entries would restate an engine default and mask the day that default narrows.

THE REAL FIX, landed in d93b118: RuntimeDependencies in VaCuus.Build.cs, UFS, extension-scoped (.rml .rcss .png .jpg .jpeg .ttf .otf under .../DevUI/.../). UBT expands the wildcards at build time into the receipt (UEBuildBinary.cs:211-219) and StageRuntimeDependenciesFromReceipt stages from it (CopyBuildToStagingDirectory.Automation.cs:1796, DeploymentContext.cs:1040-1056). Extension-scoping is deliberate: RuntimeDependencies bypasses the cooker, so a blanket Content/DevUI/... is how a .uasset gets staged raw.

VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY: built the game target and read VcHost.target -- all six loose files present as UFS, including both subdirectories and the two new m2 files.
NOT VERIFIED: a full cook+stage+pak run actually opening them at runtime. The receipt (the exact input staging consumes) and the source chain were verified; an end-to-end package was out of time budget.
close_reason: See the note added to this bead: the PREMISE was wrong and the fix is elsewhere. FilterPlugin.ini has exactly one consumer in the entire engine (RunUAT BuildPlugin) and could never have affected a cooked game. Fixed in Task 14 (d93b118) with RuntimeDependencies in VaCuus.Build.cs, extension-scoped, verified by building the game target and finding all six loose DevUI files in VcHost.target as UFS. A full cook+stage+pak was not run -- the receipt, which is staging's exact input, was.

title: FVaCuusEngine single-owner contract vs multi-PIE (spec §13 mitigation)
description: Task 3 quality review: FVaCuusEngine's owner-thread contract hard-crashes (checkf) if a second thread initializes while another owns it. Spec §4/§13 assume one UI thread per GameInstance subsystem (per PIE instance) and list 'PIE multi-instance' as mitigated by a 2-client automation test — as written, the second PIE client's UI thread would kill the process. Task 4 must either scope the engine per-subsystem or the spec's multi-PIE story must be amended. Decide during Task 4.
close_reason: Landed in m2-ui-thread a714a7b (Task 4): process-wide UI thread owned by FVaCuusModule + per-view contexts via UVaCuusSubsystem/UVaCuusView (6.10 structural, proven by new VaCuus.Threading.MultiView test); module now stops the thread it owns before engine teardown, ForceShutdownAll demoted to last-resort (6.11); vacuus.M1HUD retries with the inline document when a VFS file load fails, reported through FVaCuusViewStatus (6.7). Spec §4/§13 amended: RmlUi's global state makes per-subsystem threads impossible.

title: ForceShutdownAll cannot stop a live UI thread it does not own
description: Task 3 quality review: FVaCuusModule::ShutdownModule -> ForceShutdownAll() force-resets RefCount and calls Rml::Shutdown() from the game thread, but the UI thread is owned by VaCuusRender's console-command state in another module. title: World-panel input processor latches all application input on the first touch
description:
Found by the mobile research (docs/research/mobile-support.md, b779983) and REPRODUCIBLE ON LINUX TODAY — no phone needed. Filed separately from the mobile beads because it is not a mobile-only defect.

MECHANISM, from source: FVaCuusWorldInputProcessor takes a latch on press and clears it when the pressed-button set empties. But GetPressedButtons() is baked into the touch event at CONSTRUCTION (Events.h:938, Events.cpp:15, SlateApplication.cpp:6832), so for a touch event the clearing predicate at VaCuusWorldInputProcessor.cpp:518 can NEVER be true. The latch therefore never releases. Worse, the processor deliberately holds no Slate capture, so none of the engine's safety nets fire, and preprocessors run BEFORE all routing — so the stuck latch swallows input for the WHOLE APPLICATION, not just our panel.

WHY IT MATTERS OUTSIDE MOBILE: -faketouches (SlateApplication.cpp:900, 5261, 6092) synthesises real touch events from mouse clicks, and any touchscreen laptop or tablet-mode device produces them natively. So a desktop customer with a touch display can hit this today.

WHY IT WAS NEVER CAUGHT: the plugin's test suite has never seen a touch event — every synthesized FPointerEvent in Tests/ uses CursorPointerIndex. That is the coverage gap the fix must close, not just the latch.

FIX SHAPE (to be designed, not prescribed): the clearing condition must not depend on a button set that touch events cannot populate; a touch-index-aware release, or a latch keyed on the same event stream that set it. THE OBSERVABLE IS THE POINT: a test that drives a touch press/release through the processor and asserts the latch releases — the suite currently cannot express that, so the fixture work is part of the bead. -faketouches gives a manual reproduction for the before/after.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
MECHANISM PINNED 2026-08-03 with every line opened, and the reason it looked correct is now known. HandleMouseButtonUpEvent releases the latch only when MouseEvent.GetPressedButtons().IsEmpty() (VaCuusWorldInputProcessor.cpp:518). That can never be true for touch: FSlateApplication::OnTouchEnded constructs the event with bPressLeftMouseButton=true (SlateApplication.cpp:6832-6845) and the touch constructor bakes PressedButtons = FTouchKeySet::StandardSet into the event's VALUE COPY (Events.h:938, Events.cpp:15) — so the set is non-empty regardless of the application's live button state.

WHY IT LOOKED RIGHT: the comment at :509-517 justifying the predicate cites SlateApplication.cpp:6100-6103, which is about the application's LIVE set, not the event copy. The load-bearing justification is wrong — which is exactly the class this project's conventions name as a critical-bug source.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT: the processor holds no Slate capture by design, so no engine safety net fires; the other ClearLatch sites (:390, :446, :601) all require the panel to have died while Tick is empty (VaCuusWorldInputProcessor.h:220); and IInputProcessor offers no touch or capture-lost hook (IInputProcessor.h:26-50). So the first tap consumes every subsequent pointer event in the application, permanently.

REPRODUCES ON LINUX TODAY: -faketouches makes FSlateApplication convert every left click into a real touch event (SlateApplication.cpp:900, 5261-5264, 6092-6095). Recorded as section 0 of docs/research/mobile-support.md.

title: Blueprint struct recompile dangles every FProperty* in a live layout
description:
ANSWERED BY EXPERIMENT in M3a Task 9 (VaCuus.Model.BlueprintRecompile). The spec's 'strong ref + rebuild' mitigation was half-fictional: the strong ref works, the rebuild exists nowhere.

MECHANISM, from source: CompileStruct's own comment says 'Recompiled UDS keep the same instance' (UserDefinedStructureCompilerUtils.cpp:595) -- so the strong reference to the UScriptStruct holds. But the FIRST thing it does to that instance is CleanAndSanitizeStruct -> DestroyChildPropertiesAndResetPropertyLinks (:512, :225) -> DestroyPropertyLinkedList, a plain 'delete FieldToDestroy' over the whole chain (Class.cpp:2117-2126). Only the DefaultValueChanged change-reason is exempt (:221-232).

So: type object SURVIVES, every FProperty* in the layout DANGLES. Verified by pointer comparison (the test never dereferences the freed property).

FAILURE MODES, worst first:
- FVaCuusModelShadow's destructor runs DestroyStruct on a buffer laid out by the OLD properties using the NEW DestructorLink -- a free of a pointer read from the wrong offset. Heap corruption, not a leak.
- Sample/Publish/ApplyUpdate dereference freed memory every frame.
- Even a correct rebuild would have to run on the UI THREAD, because RmlUi holds a raw void* into the UI shadow and revalidates it never.

SCOPE: editor-only -- FStructureEditorUtils lives in UnrealEd, so a packaged game cannot reach this. Requires a designer editing a Blueprint struct while a view bound over that struct is live.

RECOMMENDED FIX IS A REFUSAL, NOT A REBUILD: have FVaCuusBoundModel register with FStructureEditorUtils::FStructEditorManager (editor-only) and, on a pre-change for its type, log an Error and stop sampling. That converts silent heap corruption into a loud, documented limitation. A real rebuild is M3b or later.
acceptance_criteria: A Blueprint struct recompiled under a live bound model produces a loud Error and a stopped model rather than dangling pointers; a test covers it.
notes: M3b doubles this hazard's surface: an array-of-struct field pins TWO type objects (model root + element type via FVaCuusModelArrayDesc::ElementLayout), and a recompile of EITHER dangles the FProperty*s a live layout holds. The tracked refusal fix must cover element types too (M3b spec §4, 2026-07-31).
close_reason: Fixed in a96ecb4 (M6 Task 2): FVaCuusStructRecompileGuard (INotifyOnStructChanged) fires at PreChange with the old property chain alive; game-thread walk matches root+ElementLayout structs; dead flag, synchronous game-shadow reset, fenced UI-side drop (observed 1.1ms vs 100ms window), Abandon() only on timeout with leaked-bytes Error; the definition registry evicts stale types so re-bind+reload is a real recovery. Two tests incl. real-UDS-rename red run.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: M6 Task-4 quality review, on record per the reviewer: the retirement design (224ffa3: Invalidate() empties the game-side Models map; UI-side refs drain via RemoveView) leaves a residual window -- a recompile whose PreChange walk condemns NOTHING returns without a fence, so a just-retired view's UI-side model refs (awaiting the already-triggered RemoveView drain) could in principle be destroyed after the struct chain is freed. When any live model IS condemned, the FIFO+fence closes the window completely (the pending RemoveView drains ahead of the drops inside PreChange). Accepted trade-off: strictly better than pre-fix, and the nothing-condemned case means no VaCuus model uses the recompiled struct, so the dangling-FProperty hazard the guard exists for is absent by construction; the destructor is thread-agnostic (no CAS, chains alive at that point).

title: M3b: data binding — arrays and data-for
description:
Split from M3 on the spec review's recommendation. The seam is real rather than administrative: a flat layout entry keyed on a byte offset cannot address an array element (its address is FScriptArrayHelper::GetRawPtr(i), valid only for the current Num()), and RmlUi dirties TOP-LEVEL NAMES ONLY, so the only granularity that maps onto DirtyVariable is one bit per top-level array -- meaning the apply deep-copies the whole array whenever any element changes.

Whether that is acceptable at 200 rows is a MEASUREMENT NOBODY HAS TAKEN, which is why this is separate: everything in M3a is settled by source already read, and everything here depends on numbers.

Carries: the array definition including the .size child (RmlUi's own array definition handles it inline; a hand-written one that forgets it breaks {{ Arr.size }} with only a warning); the bit-granularity decision; the shrink cost (RmlUi's view cleanup is self-flagged quadratic, and shrink is the expensive direction while growth appends at the tail); a 200-row budget; and the killfeed end to end.
close_reason: Merged to master f0eb3a6. TArray UPROPERTYs drive data-for end to end (killfeed demo verified on screen); one bit per array shipped on measured evidence (0.423 ms RmlUi re-evaluation vs 0.014 ms copies at 200x4); SyncCopy warm republish allocates exactly zero (counting-allocator proof, restore-the-bug showed 600 reallocs/window through the engine copy); .size child + element definitions + three evaluation counters; idle exact 0/0/0; 80 tests green x4 runs, monolithic build green, SIGTERM teardown clean with live array models.

title: CreateView returns a valid-looking handle even when UI-thread Initialize() failed
description:
Found during M3 research. CreateView returns the UVaCuusView unconditionally. If the host's Initialize() then fails on the UI thread, the host is dropped -- but the handle the caller is holding still reports IsViewValid() == true, forever.

So a caller that correctly checks the handle gets a view that will never render, never accept input and never load a document, with no way to discover this from the API. Every subsequent command it enqueues is dropped by the unknown-view-id path in DrainCommands, which logs at Verbose.

This becomes more visible in M3: a data model bound to such a view will accept updates on the game thread and silently never apply them, which is indistinguishable from the dirty-variable bug M3 must already guard against -- so two different root causes present identically.

Fix shape: the view already has an async status channel (FVaCuusViewStatus) that the load path uses to echo results back; a failed Initialize should travel the same way and flip the handle to invalid.
acceptance_criteria: A view whose UI-thread Initialize fails reports invalid through the handle, and a test covers it.
close_reason: Fixed in 0eb0033 (M6 Task 1): BootState atomic on FVaCuusViewStatus; PollStatus on first Failed logs one Error, Invalidates, fires OnLoadCompleted(false). Restore-the-bug showed the eternal-pending state verbatim (valid forever, callback never). VaCuus.View.BootFailure.

title: Snapshot focusability is an under-approximation, not RmlUi's exact precondition
description: bAnyFocusable is accumulated during the snapshot walk, but Visit returns early for vacuus-passthrough and for an empty child clip, and RmlUi's CanFocusElement (ElementDocument.cpp:30-44) knows about neither. So bTabEntersFocus is a strict UNDER-approximation: a document whose only focusables sit inside a passthrough wrapper, or inside a collapsed overflow:hidden height:0 container, reports 'Tab cannot enter' while RmlUi enters fine -- and the entering key then double-acts. Fails toward the pre-Task-14 behaviour, so not a regression. Filed because VaCuusInteractiveSnapshot.h:350 claims the flags are 'EXACTLY RmlUi's OWN PRECONDITIONS, both of them', which they are not. Mirror finding: the walk passes include_non_dom_elements=true while SearchFocusSubtreeChildren uses the default false, so a non-DOM element with tab-index auto would be a false POSITIVE -- no such element could be constructed (only ElementFormControl.cpp:8 sets TabIndex::Auto, and those are DOM).
close_reason:
Done in 6a32d47. bTabEntersFocus now matches CanFocusElement's reachability. Rather than teach the rect DFS about tab rules -- the two concerns are genuinely different traversals -- the question got its own walk mirroring RmlUi 1:1 (CanFocusElement :30-44, SearchFocusSubtree :728-737, SearchFocusSubtreeChildren :739-750), with the comment showing why FindNextTabElement(document, forward, wrap_around=true) reduces to exactly one SearchFocusSubtreeChildren call when the DOCUMENT holds focus (:675, :679-681, :691, :721, :725) -- which also means the document element itself is correctly not a candidate. Runs at most once per frame, only in the state the flag is read in, early-outs on the first target.

Restore-the-bug: reverting only VaCuusInteractiveSnapshot.cpp fails VaCuus.Input.TabReach on EXACTLY three of seven cases and no others -- the passthrough wrapper, the collapsed overflow:hidden container, and the non-DOM child. focus:none, display:none and both controls stayed green, so the test is not 'everything true'.

THE PREVIOUS REVIEWER WAS REFUTED on the non-DOM false positive, and it was real. Their premise held (ElementFormControl.cpp:8 is RmlUi's only TabIndex::Auto setter and its subclasses are all parsed from RML) but the conclusion did not: tab-index is an ordinary registered property (StyleSheetSpecification.cpp:375) and non-DOM elements are style-matched like any other, so ONE LINE of author RCSS constructs one. The test does it -- <progress> appends its fill as a non-DOM child (ElementProgress.cpp:24-27), and 'fill { tab-index: auto; }' produced a document the old code called tabbable and RmlUi provably cannot tab into. The mirror now uses GetNumChildren()'s default include_non_dom_elements=false, matching :741, so it is unreachable rather than unlikely.

Also fixed a SEVENTH comment asserting a mechanism that does not hold, found in the same file: the header said EVaCuusRectFlags::Focusable is 'computed with RmlUi's own rule' for click-focus. It is not -- a click resolves through FindFocusElement, which walks up to the nearest ancestor-or-self with focus != none and NEVER looks at tab-index (Context.cpp:607-619, :631-641), so a click on a plain div does take RmlUi focus. The flag's behaviour is right (Slate keyboard focus is the thing being gated, and stealing the player's keyboard on a background-panel click is what D11 prevents); the comment now describes it as the deliberate narrower policy it is. No behaviour changed.

title: Decide: should a digitized left-stick press enter the UI nav grid at all?
description:
Surfaced and ASSERTED (not fixed) by Task 14's acceptance work, deliberately left for a decision with real gamepad hardware.

CURRENT BEHAVIOUR: SVaCuusWidget::OnKeyDown enqueues unconditionally, so a Gamepad_LeftStick_Up/Down/Left/Right key is FORWARDED into RmlUi's nav grid and moves UI focus -- but Task 14's new rule does not CONSUME it, so the game sees it too. That is exactly the double-action the new rule removes for the DPad, on the key family where a walking player is most exposed.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED: the only clean suppression mechanism is D12's pass-through FKey set, which is static and cannot be state-dependent. Suppressing the enqueue would mean a pad player can no longer enter a VaCuus menu with the stick AT ALL -- the analog nav path is gated on bWantsKeyboardFocus (the fix for the M2 critical bug where a held movement stick silently re-focused the HUD and ate player movement), so this accident is currently the ONLY stick-based entry into the UI.

So the choice is: 'a walking player can lose the stick to UI focus' versus 'a pad player must use the DPad to enter a menu'. Both are real costs and it is a design call, not a code call.

MITIGATING CONTEXT worth weighing: OnKeyDown only runs while the widget holds SLATE KEYBOARD FOCUS, which arrives only from a click on a focusable rect or from the game deliberately putting it there. So the exposed scenario is narrower than 'player walking around' -- it is 'the UI already has keyboard focus, nothing inside the document is focused yet, and the player pushes the stick'. Most games do let the left stick drive menu navigation, which argues for keeping it.

VaCuus.Input.NavEntry asserts the CURRENT behaviour, so it will fail loudly whichever way this is decided -- the decision cannot be made silently.
design: Revisit with real gamepad hardware in the M6 platform matrix. If suppression wins, it needs a state-dependent mechanism, not the static pass-through set.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded with its reasoning, the test updated to assert it, and the losing option's cost stated in the code comment.
close_reason: Decided + implemented in a96ecb4 (M6 Task 2): digitized left-stick presses do NOT enter the nav grid by default; vacuus.NavStickPress cvar opt-in at the WIDGET site (a map-site gate would starve the analog-repeat clock — recorded); routing test asserts both ways.

title: Task 12 quality review: buffer-level gate blind spot, per-view observability, two dangerous stale comments
description:
From the Task 12 code-quality review. APPROVED WITH MINOR ISSUES -- no demonstrable bug -- but four items worth doing before M2 closes.

I1 (the important one). bHasResourceTraffic hard-codes the four arrays with NO compile-time link to FVaCuusCommandBuffer's member list. This is the buffer-level analogue of the FVaCuusCommand blind spot and it is CLOSER: the command struct is at least pinned by a static_assert; the buffer's member list is pinned by nothing, and the gate names the four arrays 500 lines from where they are declared.

The trigger is concrete, not hypothetical. The recorder overrides 9 of Rml::RenderInterface's 21 virtuals. The 12 it does not include CompileShader/RenderShader/ReleaseShader (RenderInterface.h:131-140 -- how RmlUi 6 renders decorator: linear-gradient), CompileFilter/ReleaseFilter (:122-125 -- filter: and backdrop-filter:), and EnableClipMask/RenderToClipMask (:78-86 -- rounded-corner clipping). A Gameface-class product needs all three, so they are M3/M4 work, not speculation. The moment one lands it brings a NewShaders/NewFilters map; sizeof(FVaCuusCommand) == 112 still holds because the payload is on the buffer; no test fails; and a document with an animated gradient publishes its first frame and then FREEZES.

Fix costs nothing: move the predicate onto the buffer as bool HasResourceTraffic() const, declared immediately below the four arrays with a comment saying a new array must be added to it. A member declared next to that comment is hard to miss.

I2. The per-view publish/skip counters are unreachable from anything but a unit test -- the recorder is only reachable through a Private host with no accessor on IVaCuusDocumentHost and no path onto FVaCuusViewStatus. Worse, this commit REMOVED the per-view publish count that existed (UVaCuusView::GetFramesPublished -> GetFramesRecorded). Concrete cost: two views, A genuinely idle and B wedged, produce one PROCESS-WIDE 'published=1 skipped=13295' line and nothing anywhere tells you which view contributed. Four lines: add std::atomic<uint64> FramesPublished to FVaCuusViewStatus, which already has the atomic block.

I3. No kill switch. The gate's failure mode is a frozen UI with no error, no ensure, no log -- and it is the first thing anyone will suspect when a UI stops updating, yet the only way to test that suspicion is a rebuild. FVaCuusPerfLog::IsEnabled() already establishes the UI-thread-readable cvar pattern. Natural home for the second-cheapest diagnostic too: a Verbose line on each idle<->active TRANSITION (not per frame).

I4 (dangerous). SVaCuusWidget.cpp:39-42 justifies ForceVolatile(true) with 'the UI thread publishes a command buffer per frame that only a paint drains'. That premise is now FALSE (1 publish per 13,296 frames) while the conclusion became MORE critical: since the RT is the only copy of an idle UI's pixels, Draw_RenderThread running every frame is the sole reason an idle UI stays on screen. A maintainer who reads this, knows about Task 12, and correctly concludes the stated reason no longer applies will remove ForceVolatile(true) -- and under Slate Global Invalidation the draw elements get cached, Draw_RenderThread stops being called, and the idle UI DISAPPEARS with nothing to bring it back. Called 'the single most dangerous stale comment in the tree right now'.

I5. VaCuusRmlDocumentHost.cpp:253-255 -- the Hide() comment is now wrong in both sentences. Hide still works (the first hidden frame's empty command list hashes differently, publishes, and Clear_Store wipes the RT), but the comment says the view 'keeps publishing frames, they are simply empty' and warns that 'skipping the frame would leave the last published content in the RT' -- which is precisely what now happens from frame two onward. A reader trusting it concludes either that hide is broken or that hidden views need exempting.

Minors: the header still says RecordAndPublishFrame 'publishes two things per frame' (now one per frame and one per change); the perf-log comment equating skipped with missing Replay samples is not arithmetic (Draw_RenderThread emits one Replay scope per PAINT regardless of how many buffers queued, so a changing UI at 220 Hz UI / 60 Hz paint gives published 220/s, Replay 60/s, skipped 0 -- the difference is coalescing); VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:353's 'one replay per frame' is no longer true; the one perf claim in the diff ('~600 out-of-line calls is a measurable slice of a 0.04 ms Record') is unmeasured and contradicted in direction by the diff's own numbers, so lead with the determinism argument instead; PublishInteractiveSnapshot is the one frame cost in no perf scope, two lines above a comment arguing that hiding costs makes the perf log lie; and the publish/skip counters are plain uint64 behind VACUUSRENDER_API getters with no thread annotation while every other entry point on the class opens with CheckOwnerThread().

Nits: IdleGateTest's 'command count is part of the frame hash' assertion cannot fail (appending a command adds 112 bytes regardless); the 'restarted view' half of the first-frame test is a tautology on a fresh recorder's NSDMI and would need the host path to test what it claims.
design: I1 is the one with a real future trigger -- do it as a member function next to the arrays, not as a better comment at the gate.
acceptance_criteria: Resource-traffic predicate lives on the buffer next to its arrays; per-view publish count observable at runtime; the two stale comments corrected; kill-switch cvar plus idle-transition Verbose line if judged worth it.
close_reason: Done in the Task 12 quality fix pass (982ec06, 1897320, 920965e). I1: the resource-traffic predicate moved onto FVaCuusCommandBuffer next to the four arrays, guarded by a member-count tripwire -- adding a fifth array without touching the predicate now FAILS THE BUILD, proven by adding one and removing it. A second site enumerating the arrays inline (the recorder's destructor) was found and re-pointed. I2: per-view FramesPublished added to FVaCuusViewStatus so an idle view can be told from a wedged one. I3: vacuus.IdleGate cvar plus a Verbose line on each idle<->active transition. I4/I5 and five minors: comments corrected. The I4 finding itself was partly refuted -- see the memory on Slate cached custom elements.

title: Task 12 review follow-ups: hash tripwire blind spot, test controls, RT-is-only-copy comment
description:
From the Task 12 spec review. Three items, the first is a latent hazard of exactly the kind this feature must not have.

1. THE HASH TRIPWIRE HAS A 7-BYTE BLIND SPOT. VaCuusCommandBuffer.h asserts sizeof(FVaCuusCommand) == 112 and offsetof(Geometry) == 8, with a message promising that an unhashed field cannot slip through. It catches a field appended after Transform, or anything that changes sizeof. It does NOT catch a field declared between Type and Geometry that fits the existing padding -- a uint8/uint16/uint32 lands at offsets 1-7, leaves sizeof at 112 and offsetof(Geometry) at 8, passes silently, and goes UNHASHED. That is precisely the 'false unchanged -> visibly stale UI with no diagnostic' failure the assert advertises preventing. Fix: four more offsetof clauses (Texture == 16, Translation == 24, Scissor == 32, Transform == 48).

2. IdleGate.HashPadding's positive controls mutate one representative scalar per field GROUP (Translation.Y, Scissor.Max.Y, Transform.M[3][1]), proving each group participates but not each of the nine scalars. A copy-paste bug of the form Image.Scissor[1] = Command.Scissor.Min.X would leave Scissor.Min.Y permanently unhashed and every assertion in the file would still pass. The nine assignments are correct today -- verified by hand -- but the test does not defend them. Fix: five more one-line mutations (Translation.X, Scissor.Min.X/Min.Y/Max.X, a second matrix cell).

3. A NEW HAZARD THE TASK INTRODUCED, worth a comment even though nothing exploits it today. Before the gate, every frame republished, so any lost or unreplayed buffer self-healed on the next frame. Now, on a static UI the render target is the ONLY copy of the pixels and the recorder will never resend them. FVaCuusReplayRenderer::ReleaseResources() resetting LastConsumedGeneration = 0 is therefore load-bearing in a way it was not before: any FUTURE path that drops the RT without also destroying the recorder, or that discards an unreplayed buffer, becomes a PERMANENTLY blank UI rather than a one-frame glitch. Put that on ReleaseResources().

Also: the comment dismissing Rml::Context::GetNextUpdateDelay as 'a timer hint' is stronger than RmlUi's header justifies -- the header presents it as an on-demand-rendering mechanism (Context.h:284-286). The real reason it cannot serve here is different and worth stating correctly: it is forward-looking, returns infinity when the answer is 'wait for input', and says nothing about whether the frame just recorded differs from the last one.
acceptance_criteria: Four offsetof clauses added so a padding-slot field fails to compile; five more scalar mutations in HashPadding; ReleaseResources carries the RT-is-the-only-copy note; the GetNextUpdateDelay comment states the accurate reason.
close_reason:
Landed in Task 13 (23f3181 exact-EOF Tell, a117ba7 private VaCuusRml dep, df2164b task-10 follow-ups, c82a2ce task-12 follow-ups, 5d0a36b self-correction). 31/31 tests green; both the editor and the MONOLITHIC game target rebuilt Succeeded, and the monolithic target genuinely recompiled Module.VaCuusRender.cpp so the dependency change was exercised rather than assumed.

6.1: verified the clamp at UnixPlatformFile.cpp:177 (FileOffset = NewPosition >= FileSize ? FileSize - 1 : NewPosition) before coding. Rml::FileHandle now carries handle + logical position + cached size; Seek moves only the position and Read re-syncs the handle. RmlUi's contract was checked in the vendored header rather than assumed POSIX. Restore-the-bug: reverting Tell() to the handle gave 4 failures (Tell 15 instead of 16; empty-file EOF reporting 18446744073709551615), and reverting the whole pre-fix pair gave 6, adding 'a read returns 0, not the last byte again'. NEW FACT WORTH KEEPING: the exact-EOF clamp is UNIX-ONLY -- both Windows read handles accept InPos == FileSize and report it -- so this fix makes Unix agree with Windows rather than inventing a third contract.

6.4: premise confirmed before acting -- zero RmlUi includes anywhere under VaCuusRender/Public/, and in fact no Build.cs in the plugin or the host project even names VaCuusRender.

6.32 (task-12 spec review): D1's stated fix WAS WRONG AND THE FINDING IS WORSE THAN STATED. A uint32 between Type and Geometry occupies offsets 4-7 and shifts nothing: sizeof stays 112 and every other member keeps its offset, so offsetof is structurally incapable of seeing it. Verified by building it both ways. What catches it is a MEMBER COUNT check -- FVaCuusCommand is an aggregate, so brace-initialising it with one initialiser too many is ill-formed inside a requires-expression. The four offset clauses were kept anyway for a different reason: they catch REORDERING (swapping Texture with Translation leaves both sizeof and the member count intact). Restore-the-bug: the padding-slot field now fails compilation with 'FVaCuusCommand gained or lost a field'; with the pre-change assert it compiled clean. D2 also got an unrequested restore-the-bug -- the exact copy-paste slip named in review now fails, and passed the whole file before.

title: Policy: first nav press is both consumed by the UI and seen by the game
description: Task 7 finding: bWantsKeyboardFocus is false while only the document holds focus (per D9), so the FIRST direction key is enqueued (moving UI focus) AND answered Unhandled (game sees it too) — in a real game the camera twitches on the first DPad press. Same for analog nav, which is deliberately emitted regardless of bWantsKeyboardFocus so the bootstrap press can reach the document. Needs a per-view 'document is up and navigable' policy bit. Decide at Task 14 acceptance, do not widen silently.
close_reason: Decided in M2 Task 14 (c6d7726): the press that ENTERS the UI's focus is consumed and not also given to the game; activation keys (Return/NumpadEnter/Space/FaceButton_Bottom) keep the old rule; digitized left-stick keys are excluded. Implemented by PREDICTING RmlUi's own preconditions rather than approximating them -- two snapshot flags, later refined to a 4-bit direction mask because 'nav' is a Box shorthand, so 'nav: vertical' declares all four directions and acts on two (an ANY-of bool swallows strafe; an ALL-of bool reintroduces the double-action). Activation keys are excluded for a checkable reason: with nothing focused they resolve to the document, which has no tab-index auto, so they do nothing and consuming them would eat a player's jump for free. The remaining left-stick question is split out as 6.35.

title: Verify snapshot-vs-input-dispatch frame ordering empirically on Linux
description: Task 5 review found the documented rationale is backwards on Linux: FLinuxApplication::AddPendingEvent dispatches input synchronously during FPlatformApplicationMisc::PumpMessages (LaunchEngineLoop.cpp:5784) — BEFORE GEngine->Tick (:5859) where PollStatus refreshes the snapshot cache — because GPumpingMessagesOutsideOfMainLoop is only ever set on Windows. So input in frame N sees the cache built in frame N-1, one frame older than VaCuusView.h claims; cursor updates (TickPlatform, later in FSlateApplication::Tick) end up fresher than mouse dispatch. The single-stable-snapshot-per-dispatch-batch property still holds. Verify empirically with log timestamps/Insights once SVaCuusWidget lands in Task 6 and correct the header rationale.
close_reason: Verified empirically on Linux during M2: input dispatches during PumpMessages, i.e. BEFORE GEngine->Tick, so the snapshot a handler reads is one frame old -- observed directly (frame 396 consuming generation 394). That ordering is why the snapshot is cached game-thread-side once per frame: every handler in a frame then sees one stable geometry instead of a moving target.

title: LoadModuleChecked on the UI thread (LoadTexture) — same hazard class as the fixed Engine::Get()
description: Task 4 found that FModuleManager::LoadModuleChecked refuses to serve a module to a non-game thread (assert NotLoadedByGameThread) — FVaCuusEngine::Get() was fixed by injecting the reference. One instance remains: FVaCuusRecordingRenderInterface::LoadTexture calls LoadModuleChecked<IImageWrapperModule>("ImageWrapper") on the UI thread (VaCuusRecordingRenderInterface.cpp:~121). Works during normal frames but is the same crash class during load/unload windows. Fix by caching the module pointer at boot from the game thread; Task 11 rewrites this path anyway.
close_reason:
Landed in Task 11 (a177662) + fix cycle (4dde61b, eebeb52). Async DECODE only -- the payload arrival travels in band through FVaCuusCommandBuffer::NewTextures rather than out of band into the replayer's map, because an out-of-band arrival would have been installed but never re-replayed once Task 12's idle gate landed. Async UPLOAD deferred to 6.25 with a measurement (~1 ms of render thread per 4 MB).

Proven end to end in a live headless PIE run, not just by unit contract: with a deliberately slow 6000x6000 decode, UI frame 3 shows the transparent 1x1 placeholder and frame 300 shows the real payload, same asset and same command. Decoding 36M pixels cost the UI thread nothing measurable (Update max 0.095 ms, indistinguishable from steady state). Zero ensures fired, including the replayer's unknown-handle ensure under exactly the condition it guards. Evidence in docs/research/proofs/m2-t11-async-texture/.

6.12 folded in: the IImageWrapperModule lookup is now cached once from the game thread in StartupModule via LoadModulePtr. The bug was real but LATENT rather than deterministic -- ModuleManager.cpp:935-939 returns an already-loaded module even off the game thread, so it would only have crashed on a session where ImageWrapper had not yet loaded when the first UI-thread LoadTexture ran.

Follow-ups filed rather than folded: 6.25 async upload, 6.26 module unload racing a decode, 6.27 unsized-view drain window, 6.28 small comment/guard fixes, 6.30 grayscale UEJPEG, and 6.31 -- a P1 that predates M1, where .bmp/.dds in a document hard-crash the editor because those wrappers check() on the requested format.

description: RmlUi Context::Render re-records every frame (no dirty tracking) — M1 publishes ~0.06ms Record + 0.03ms Replay every frame even for static UI. title: Mobile research: what VaCuus actually needs before iOS is a supported platform
description:
RESEARCH ONLY, no implementation — the owner's scope for now is 'only research of tasks within Epic's platforms'. The Mac has the engine's IOS platform extension installed (Engine/Platforms/IOS, Engine/Binaries/IOS, Source/Runtime/Core/Private/{IOS,Apple}), and Xcode 26.0 is present, so the toolchain half is closer than Android's.

Shares most of its risk surface with VaCuus-ma3 (Android) — research them together and only record what genuinely DIFFERS here. The iOS-specific items:

1. JIT IS FORBIDDEN. iOS refuses W^X: no writable-executable pages for third-party apps. quickjs-ng is an interpreter and should be fine, but this must be CONFIRMED from the vendored source rather than assumed — check for any code path that allocates executable memory, and check what our JS_SetGCThreshold/stack handling does. If anything JITs, iOS is blocked outright, and that changes the product's shape.
2. Metal only, and mobile Metal at that (ES3_1-equivalent feature level by default). Our custom pass, the .usf shaders, the composite permutation and the MD_UI material pair all need their ShouldCompilePermutation gates checked against iOS shader platforms. The macOS pass already proved the DESKTOP Metal path works at SM5 and that glass takes the bounded-copy fallback because Metal does not set ShaderResource on the Slate output — mobile Metal is likely stricter still.
3. MEMORY-MAPPED BUNDLE IS LIVE ON iOS: IOSPlatformProperties::SupportsMemoryMappedFiles() returns TRUE. Same never-executed code as Android — and on iOS the file-mapping and paging rules are their own subject.
4. Touch input and the iOS virtual keyboard — same gap as Android but a different API surface.
5. THE DEDICATED UI THREAD under iOS app lifecycle: backgrounding, suspension, and the OS's willingness to kill a process holding threads. Our UI thread owns every Rml::Context process-wide; what happens on suspend/resume has never been considered.
6. Provisioning/signing and what a plugin must declare to ship through the App Store — plus whether test automation can run on device at all.
7. Bitcode/arm64e, and whether any vendored third party (RmlUi, quickjs-ng, FreeType via the engine) has an iOS-specific build story.

DELIVERABLE: a research note under docs/research/ — per area: works unchanged / needs work with an estimate / blocked, each claim citing engine or plugin source. Then this bead splits into implementation beads.

The iOS-specific good news from the research, so it is not re-litigated: quickjs is CLEAR — zero mmap/mprotect/MAP_JIT/dlopen hits in the whole vendored tree, so no JIT, no entitlement needed, nothing to disable. That was the one item that could have blocked iOS outright, and it does not.

title: Mobile research: what VaCuus actually needs before Android is a supported platform

THE OWNER'S HYPOTHESIS, to be tested rather than assumed: 'apart from mipmap generation and small things, everything should work on mobile'. Several areas suggest it is optimistic; the deliverable is the honest inventory with file:line, not a verdict.

Risk areas to research, each answered from Epic's own platform sources:
1. RHI/feature level — ES3_1 vs SM5 on Android Vulkan/GLES. Our custom replay pass, the .usf shaders and their permutations (VaCuusUIShaders, the composite LinearOutput permutation, VaCuusMaterialDraw's MD_UI FMaterialShader pair): do their ShouldCompilePermutation gates admit mobile shader platforms, and does the mobile renderer even run our ICustomSlateElement path?
2. FGenerateMips on mobile — WillFormatSupportCompute and whether ES3_1 has the compute path at all (the world-panel mips work assumes it).
3. THE MEMORY-MAPPED BUNDLE PATH IS LIVE ON ANDROID. AndroidPlatformProperties::SupportsMemoryMappedFiles() returns TRUE (unlike Linux/macOS, where the generic false sends us down the resident-buffer path). So BULKDATA_MemoryMappedPayload executes for the first time on this platform — code that has never run anywhere.
4. Input — our path is mouse/keyboard/gamepad. Touch does not map today; what does Slate deliver on Android and what would a pointer bridge cost?
5. Text entry — the mobile virtual keyboard is a different model from ITextInputMethodSystem entirely.
6. The dedicated UI thread on a phone: core counts, thread priorities, what UE does about background/foreground transitions and app suspension (our UI thread owns every Rml::Context process-wide).
7. quickjs-ng: interpreter only, no JIT — confirm from the vendored source, and confirm Android has no W^X objection.
8. Glass/backdrop blur: it needs the scene colour; check what the mobile renderer exposes.
9. Packaging/toolchain: what Android needs (SDK/NDK/JDK versions the engine pins), and what the .uplugin/Build.cs must declare — the descriptor currently names no SupportedTargetPlatforms and no PlatformAllowList, i.e. it claims every platform including ones never built.
10. Whether anything in the plugin is Win64/desktop-only by construction (the bundle's mmap branch, VaCuusEditor, the world-panel material preset).

title: World panels: visibility-driven throttle for the UI pipeline (mass in-scene UI)
description:
Filed 2026-08-02 from the owner's question "does an off-screen world panel tick/render?" — the honest answer exposed the gap this bead closes. Matters at MASS in-scene UI scale (name plates, kiosks, terminals: tens-hundreds of panels), where cost scales with panel COUNT, not with visible count.

CURRENT STATE, verified with opened lines:
- The component never ticks by design (VaCuusWorldComponent.cpp:146) — zero tick cost either way.
- The mesh draw IS visibility-culled by the engine: bDrawRelevance = IsShown(View), CanBeOccluded() (VaCuusWorldComponent.cpp:121,130; occlusion query measured 0.47 us in the M5 manual matrix).
- The UI PIPELINE IS NOT: the view Updates + Records on the UI thread every UI frame, JS runs, and each publish drives replay + CopyTexture into the panel RT (+ FGenerateMips as of branch worldpanel-mips, 3da3a82) on the render thread — none of it consults camera visibility. The only throttle is the CONTENT-driven idle gate (WS-COPY-COST, VaCuusWorldComponent.h: 2 publishes / 13,074 recorded frames on a static HUD).
- WORST CASE is a material-decorator document: forced republish clamped to engine rate — such a panel replays+copies+generates EVERY engine frame while completely unseen. This is the biggest single win for the throttle.

DESIGN FORKS to decide (each needs its cost stated):
1. SIGNAL: WasRecentlyRendered(threshold) (engine-maintained LastRenderTime from the proxy, game-thread cheap) vs proxy visibility callbacks (occlusion-precise) vs distance tiers (LOD-style). WasRecentlyRendered is the cheap default; note it goes true from ANY view rendering the panel (shadow/capture passes may count — verify).
2. PAUSE SEMANTICS — the core fork:
   (a) full view pause (Update+JS+Record stop): maximum saving; JS timers freeze and the panel either jumps or visibly catches up on re-show;
   (b) publish-side suspension (Update+JS keep running, Record/publish/copy/mips skipped): saves the render side (~0.4 ms Record at reference scale + replay + copy + mips) and re-shows instantly current — but UI-thread cost remains, so it does NOT solve mass scale;
   (c) rate throttle (e.g. 5 Hz when unseen): bounded staleness, partial saving, no freeze pathologies.
   At mass scale (a) or (c) is the answer; (b) is the safe incremental step.
3. RE-SHOW: the RT is the ONLY copy of the pixels (idle-gate invariant — a dropped publish is permanently stale, see the akj.6.32/6.33 lessons on ReleaseResources). A pause must end with a forced publish-on-wake, and the first frame after re-show is stale until it lands — decide whether that is acceptable (likely yes at distance) and TEST it.
4. INPUT: the world input processor traces against the panel roster; a paused panel should still resolve traces or explicitly refuse — decide and assert (the processor's occlusion rule already handles occluded-but-live panels).
5. THREADING: the visibility signal is game-thread state; pausing the view must cross to the UI thread as an enqueued command per the standing thread invariant. The flag-crossing pattern from SetGenerateMips (worldpanel-mips) is the template.
6. MASS-SCALE ENDGAME (may split into its own bead at implementation time): a global budget scheduler — N panel updates per frame, round-robin over visible panels, unseen panels at floor rate; per-panel RDG builders for mips may want batching at that point.

ACCEPTANCE SHAPE (for whoever implements): every fork above gets a recorded decision; the throttle state is OBSERVABLE (per-panel suspended-frame counter + a PerfLog line — an invariant with no observable will rot); tests include the re-show staleness case and a restore-the-bug on the wake-publish; the material-decorator worst case measured before/after; the perf-guide world-panel section gains the numbers.

title: data-style-* bindings with units defeat the idle gate on every dirty
description:
Found while measuring M3a's acceptance. This is RmlUi behaviour, not ours, but it changes what a HUD author pays and it is invisible to them.

DataViewStyle::Update compares p->Get<String>() against the expression's string (DataViewDefault.cpp:168), and Property::Get<T>() returns the raw variant WITHOUT THE UNIT (Property.h:41-45). So '100' never equals '100%': SetProperty runs on EVERY dirty, layout is invalidated, and the frame republishes even when the bound value did not change.

Consequence for the acceptance numbers, worth recording: this is why one implementer's MarkEveryFieldDirty restore-the-bug run failed the RENDER-level idle gate while an earlier text-only one did not. The spec's claim stands -- for {{text}} and data-attr the render-level test genuinely cannot discriminate, which is exactly why the apply-level assertion exists -- but the render-level test's blindness is VIEW-KIND-DEPENDENT, and that is worth knowing before anyone trusts it alone.

Practical impact: any data-style-* binding whose value carries a unit (%, px, em) costs a relayout per dirty, forever, whether or not the value moved. A HUD with a data-style-bound progress width would never go idle.

Options: document it as a authoring guideline; or normalise the comparison on our side before dirtying; or upstream a fix to RmlUi (the comparison should include the unit).
acceptance_criteria: Either the behaviour is documented where a HUD author will meet it, or the comparison is normalised so a data-style binding with an unchanged value does not relayout.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-08-03 (42c213e). The code half landed as a ONE-LINE patch to the vendored tree, after the other two options were proven impossible rather than merely undesirable: (1) normalization at our binding layer has NO HOOK — Factory::RegisterDataViewInstancer refuses a duplicate name and warns (Factory.cpp:561-567) so 'style' cannot be shadowed, Element::SetProperty is not virtual (Element.h:177) so no custom instancer can intercept, and DataModel::DirtyVariable takes top-level names only so the coarse dirty cannot be narrowed; (2) an authoring rule + lint CANNOT COVER IT — a percentage bar cannot be written without its unit (the shipped reference HUD itself binds data-style-width="Health + '%'"), and the common shape carries the unit in a UPROPERTY at runtime, invisible to any static check, so the shipped advice 'bind unit-less numbers' was unfollowable. THE FIX: DataViewStyle::Update compares p->ToString() instead of p->Get<String>() — Property::Get<T> forwards to the value Variant (Property.h:41-45) while the unit is a separate member (:50-51), so '120px' read back as '120' and never compared equal. The fork's real danger is a silent re-vendor, so it is recorded the quickjs-ng way: a new Source/ThirdParty/RmlUi/VENDORED_TAG.txt with mechanism, diff, re-vendor procedure and the named verification. VENDORED_SHA.txt deliberately untouched — Tools/gen_rcss_matrix.py:134 reads that whole file and strips it into a generated doc, so a bare SHA is a machine contract. The doc half shipped earlier in docs/buyer/perf-guide.md.

title: RunFrame() has no perf scope: DrainCommands and DrainInput are unmeasured
description:
Found during M3 research. The UI thread's RunFrame() carries no VACUUS_PERF_SCOPE at all, so two substantial pieces of per-frame work are outside every measurement the project has:

- DrainCommands does full document parse and layout on a load
- DrainInput does hit-testing, focus resolution and IME work

This is the UI-thread twin of bead 6.38 (game-thread work outside the scopes), and it matters more now, because M3's per-frame data-model apply lands exactly there. Without a scope, the milestone's own cost cannot be attributed: an apply that costs 0.3 ms would be invisible, and the spec's UI-thread budget row would keep reporting Update+Record only.

Add the scope before M3's apply lands, so the apply's cost is measurable from the first commit rather than retrofitted.
acceptance_criteria: RunFrame's phases are covered by perf scopes; the M3 data apply has its own scope; stat vacuus and the PerfLog distinguish it from Update and Record.
close_reason: Closed as done: RunFrame carries VACUUS_PERF_SCOPE for DrainCommands/DrainInput/DataApply/JsPump/JsGC; stats declared and PerfLog prints every phase (verified in M6 research, p2-sweep.md).

title: RmlUi asserts are compiled out — but its ERROR LOGS are not (premise corrected)
description:
Found during M3 API research, verified through the whole chain:

UBT defines NDEBUG=1 (UEBuildPlatform.cs:1344) -> RMLUI_DEBUG is left undefined (Platform.h:20-21) -> every RmlUi assert is a no-op (Debug.h:45-52). And because RMLUI_LOG_TYPE_ERROR is defined as RMLUI_ERRORMSG (DataTypes.h:74), this silences not just asserts but RmlUi's ERROR-level LOGGING as well.

So in every build we ship or test, the vendored library's entire self-diagnosis is absent. The worst instance found so far is in the data-binding type registry: double-registering a struct returns StructHandle<T>(nullptr, nullptr) SILENTLY, and the next RegisterMember call null-derefs (DataStructHandle.h:125). A crash with no preceding diagnostic, where upstream RmlUi would have told you exactly what you did wrong.

This is not an M3 problem -- it applies to M1 and M2 code already shipped, and to every future milestone. Two things worth deciding:

(a) Should a Development/Debug editor build define RMLUI_DEBUG so the library's own asserts fire during development? That is a one-line Build.cs change, and it would have caught unknown numbers of misuse at authoring time rather than as a crash. Cost: RmlUi's asserts abort rather than ensure, so a misuse becomes a hard stop instead of a wrong picture -- which is arguably what you want in Development.

(b) Independently: anywhere VaCuus calls an RmlUi API whose only failure signal is an assert, VaCuus should check the precondition itself and log through LogVaCuus. Those call sites need finding.

Filed at the plugin level rather than under a milestone because it spans all of them.
design: Prefer (b) for anything already shipped, and evaluate (a) as a development-only define. Do not enable RMLUI_DEBUG in Shipping -- abort-on-misuse is not shippable behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on (a); and the call sites where VaCuus relies on an RmlUi API whose only failure signal is a compiled-out assert are enumerated and guarded.
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-07-31 by the M3a pre-merge review, which read Log.cpp rather than inheriting the claim. The original title and description were WRONG on the half that mattered most.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: Rml::Log::Message is an ordinary function that forwards to the registered SystemInterface (Log.cpp:11-31), and VaCuus's own system interface routes LT_ERROR -> UE_LOG(LogVaCuus, Error) and LT_WARNING -> Warning (VaCuusSystemInterface.cpp:73-78). So RmlUi's error and warning LOGGING reaches our log in every configuration.

Only RMLUI_ASSERT / RMLUI_ASSERTMSG / RMLUI_ERROR are compiled out (Debug.h:45-50, gated on RMLUI_DEBUG, which Platform.h:20-21 defines only when NDEBUG is absent).

WHERE THE CONFUSION CAME FROM: the macro RMLUI_LOG_TYPE_ERROR really is defined as the assert macro -- but it exists in only three headers (DataModelHandle.h, DataTypeRegister.h, DataStructHandle.h), i.e. the TEMPLATED type-registration path. M3a's design deliberately bypasses that path entirely via BindCustomDataVariable. So the one place the original claim held is the one place this plugin does not go.

CONSEQUENCE FOR M3a: the milestone's named signature failure is NOT silent. Element.cpp:2218 emits 'Could not locate data model %s in element %s' at LT_ERROR, which lands as 'LogVaCuus: Error: [Rml] Could not locate data model...'. Nine code comments, the M3 spec section 8, and several of my own briefs repeat the false version; being corrected in the M3a fix pass.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND STILL WORTH DOING: RmlUi's asserts are absent, so any API whose ONLY failure signal is an assert still needs VaCuus to check its own precondition. That is now the whole of this issue, hence the priority drop from P2 to P3 -- the diagnostic blackout is far narrower than filed.

title: PerfLog TickLog sorts an unbounded array on the game thread holding the shared lock
description: TickLog appends each window into a Cumulative array forever, then re-copies and re-sorts the WHOLE cumulative array every 5 s for 7 scopes -- on the game thread, holding State.Lock, which is the same lock the UI thread takes in Update/Record and the render thread in Replay/Composite. At 500 input events/s over ten minutes that is roughly a 30 ms sort per window with two other threads stalled behind it. cvar-gated off by default and deliberately outside SlateTick, so the tool's own cost is invisible to the numbers it produces -- which also means 'the measurements already include the lock' is true of the ACQUISITION but not of the contention the tool itself creates.

description: The three scopes added in Task 14 (GameTick, SlateTick, Input) do not cover the whole game-thread path, so the budget gate is met by inference from a 25x margin rather than by complete measurement -- recorded that way in spec 11. Outside all scopes: SVaCuusWidget::OnPaint (per frame, per view, includes an ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND with a lambda allocation), OnMouseEnter/OnMouseLeave/OnMouseCaptureLost (no Input scope), and OnFocusReceived/OnFocusLost (OnFocusReceived does a MakeShared, a global SetNavigationConfig, a ToString() and a nav-direction probe).
